ShortDescription.Value: Fixes the tourism simulation: tourists actually arrive by plane and ferry, demand scales with your city, hotels fill up, and the numbers finally mean something.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Tourism Overhaul
Cities: Skylines II ships tourism with several defects that make the whole feature feel inert. You can max out city attractiveness and still see almost no visitors. This mod fixes the causes.
Every change was derived by decompiling and tracing the game's own assemblies, not by guesswork. The full trace, with the file and line behind each finding, is on the GitHub page.
## Tourists actually arrive
The base game picks each tourist's transport mode with one random roll — 10% road, 10% train, 50% air, 30% sea — then looks for an outside connection of exactly that type. If your city doesn't have one, it gives up. No fallback, no retry. But the tourist household is still created, just without a location, and a household with no location can never be given any people. It's silently deleted moments later.
On a city with no airport and no harbour, that destroys 80% of all tourist arrivals.
This mod redistributes the share across the connection types your city actually has, and keeps the intended preference for planes and ferries once you build an airport or harbour.
## Arrivals route around congestion
The base game has no capacity concept for outside connections at all. A saturated airport keeps receiving its full share, and any tourist who can't travel onward from it is deleted rather than rerouted.
This mod watches how many tourists are still waiting at each entrance and shifts arrivals toward routes that are moving. Build a harbour and it starts carrying real traffic.
## Tourism scales with your city
The base game targets attractiveness x 15 tourists, and attractiveness itself is capped at 100 — a flat 1,500 visitors whether you're a town or a metropolis. Past that ceiling, every extra park and landmark does nothing at all.
This mod scales the target with population, so a large attractive city supports a proportionate number of visitors. Fully tunable, with a safety ceiling.
## Tourists have a real length of stay
The game declares a tourist departure timer, saves it, and never reads it. It also has a function returning a random stay length that nothing ever calls. Both are unfinished.
This mod implements the mechanic using the field the game already has, so visits have a believable duration and turnover instead of guests lingering until their money runs out.
## The numbers finally mean something
The tourism panel computes a figure around eight times larger than the simulation can ever produce, and its tourist count ignores everyone travelling between destinations.
This mod reports the real values and adds three rows to the Tourism info view:
- Tourists in city — current against the number your city can sustain - Hotel rooms free — free against total, across every hotel - Local cims away — your own residents currently on holiday elsewhere
## Optional extras
- Hotel room multiplier, 1x to 10x, for zoned commercial hotels. Signature buildings keep their authored capacity. - Residents take holidays. The base game suppresses out-of-town travel to roughly 1-3% of leisure trips and blocks it entirely for households with no spare money. Turn this up and your citizens will use your airport too. - A coloured ring marker under tourists so you can pick them out of a crowd, with adjustable colour and size.
Everything is individually toggleable, and everything is off or at vanilla values by default except the arrival fixes.
## Compatibility
No Harmony patches and no reflection. Arrivals use real outside connections, real vehicles, real pathfinding, real hotels and the real economy. Safe to add to an existing save, and safe to remove.
The optional hotel room multiplier replaces the game's lodging system with a copy that applies the multiplier — this is unavoidable, because room count is computed inside a compiled job from values that also control rent and workplaces. Turning the setting off restores the original system immediately. Leave it off if you'd rather nothing native is replaced.
Source, full technical writeup and issue tracker: https://github.com/Meapy/CS2-TourismOverhaul
Publish.ChangeLog:
Initial release.
- Fixes tourist arrivals being discarded when the city has no airport or harbour. - Reroutes arrivals away from congested outside connections. - Scales tourist demand with city size instead of capping at 1500. - Implements the unused length-of-stay timer. - Optional hotel room multiplier. - Optional resident holidays out of the city. - Adds tourists in city, hotel rooms free and local cims away to the Tourism info view. - Optional coloured ring marker on tourists.
